title: Michal helped David escape through a window.
paragraphs: Michal helped David escape through a window.
Then one day, she looked at that same man dancing before the Lord… and despised him in her heart.
Read that again.

She once protected the anointed king.
Later, she mocked the worshiper.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You can be close to God’s purpose and still let your heart grow cold toward God’s presence.
Michal’s story is tragic because it starts with courage and ends with contempt.
In 1 Samuel 19, she risked herself to save David from Saul’s murderous rage. She saw the cost. She saw the danger. She acted. In that moment, Michal looked like an ally to God’s plan.
But in 2 Samuel 6, when David returned dancing before the Lord with all his might, Michal didn’t see worship.

She saw embarrassment.
She saw weakness.
She saw something beneath royal dignity.
And that was the revealing.
Because what comes out of us in holy moments exposes what rules us in secret.

David was overwhelmed by the presence of God.
Michal was consumed with the image of man.
That is still the battle now.

Some people will help God’s servant when it feels strategic…
but despise surrender when it looks undignified.

Some will stand beside the calling…
but recoil at true brokenness before the Lord.
And some of you reading this have done the same thing in quieter ways.

You admired Jesus when He sounded powerful.
But stumbled when He demanded repentance.

You liked the blessing.
But resisted the bowing.

You wanted the crown.
But not the cross.
That is where sin always exposes us.

Sin is not only rebellion in the streets.
Sometimes it is pride in the palace.

Sometimes it wears dignity.
Sometimes it speaks with polished words.
Sometimes it mocks wholehearted devotion because wholehearted devotion threatens the ego.

Michal despised David.
But deeper still, she despised what David’s worship revealed about her own heart.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is the part many skip too quickly: outward proximity to God’s work does not equal inward surrender to God’s Son.
And that is why behavior modification is never enough.

You do not need better optics.
You need a new heart.

Here’s the early truth many avoid:
without Christ, even our noblest moments are stained by pride, self-preservation, and hidden resistance to God. Surface insight helps, but transformation goes further:

Jesus is the answer Michal needed.
Jesus is the answer you need.

Because the real problem is not merely that we have mocked what is holy.
It is that sin has separated us from a holy God.
But God, in His mercy, sent His Son.

Jesus Christ lived the sinless life we could not live.
He died on the cross for sinners.
He bore wrath in the place of the guilty.
He rose again in victory.
And now forgiveness, grace, and redemption are offered—not to the proud who justify themselves—but to those who repent and believe.

This is the Gospel:
your sin is real,
your pride is deadly,
your self-rule cannot save you,
but Jesus Christ receives the repentant and makes sinners new.

That means the end of your story does not have to be contempt.
It can be cleansing.

It can be surrender.
It can be joy.
It can be worship without shame.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.

Maybe you have been near truth for years but far from surrender.
Maybe you have criticized what you secretly needed.
Maybe you have looked at wholehearted worship and called it foolish because your heart was never fully yielded.

But here’s the mercy:
Jesus still saves the proud who repent.

Come down from the throne of self.
Turn from sin.
Trust in Christ alone.
And then worship Him—not for appearance, not for applause, but because He is worthy.
Follow the source, not the fragments:
So here is the question:

Are you helping around the anointing…
while secretly despising the humility true worship requires?
